inputs.statement: For finite index types ι and ι′ related by an equivalence, and coordinatewise volume measures on finite-dimensional real Pi spaces, reindexing coordinates by the equivalence preserves volume.

hypotheses: f is an equivalence between the index types.
Each coordinate carries its volume measure and the coordinate volume measures are sigma-finite.

argument.text: At time r set g_j=u_t·u_{x_j}. Smoothness and compact support give continuous compactly supported derivatives, so they are integrable by M001. For each j, reindex the finite Pi-coordinate family ℝ^n by the bijection separating coordinate j from the other n−1 coordinates; M010 states that this coordinate reindexing preserves volume. Thus the spatial measure is the product of Lebesgue measure on the remaining coordinates and on the jth coordinate. On each coordinate line integrate by parts with M007, taking v=1; the boundary values of g_j vanish, so the line integral of ∂_j g_j is zero. M003 applies to the product-integrable reindexed derivative and identifies its whole-space integral with the iterated line integral, giving ∫∂_j g_j=0. Expanding the product derivative yields ∫u_{x_j}·∂_j u_t=−∫u_t·u_{x_jx_j}. Summing over j and differentiating the finite Frobenius energy sum gives ∫e_t=2∫u_t·(u_{tt}−Δ_xu). The already established identity E′(r)=∫e_t(x,r)dx therefore gives E′(r)=2∫u_t·(u_{tt}−Δ_xu).
